hypothesis: Light eth_call is ~47% futex wait/wake on tokio's blocking pool (one shared Mutex + Condvar per spawn, finish and park) with up to 256 calls in flight (--rpc.max-blocking-io-requests default). Capping in-flight blocking IO at 8 (~cores on an 8-vCPU box) queues extra requests on reth's async semaphore instead, shrinking the pool and its lock contention. Same build as the champion; config only.
llm_commentary: Capping in-flight blocking IO at 8 (--rpc.max-blocking-io-requests=8, verified in the on-box wrapper and accepted by the node) on the champion build gives 4.97s [4.99/5.03/4.88] vs 5.00s [4.99/5.01/4.98]: no measurable change. eth_call does take that semaphore (rpc-eth-api helpers/call.rs:308), so the cap was active; the light phase's ~47% futex wait/wake is per-call handoff cost (tokio blocking-pool lock + condvar signal + worker wakeup, then the oneshot wakeup back to the async task), which every call pays regardless of how many are in flight. Fewer permits only move the queueing onto the async semaphore. Cutting it needs a cheaper handoff for short calls (a dedicated pool with per-worker queues, or running cheap calls without the blocking-pool round trip), which is a design change rather than a config knob; 16/32 were skipped because 8 already bounds the effect.
